on_record.summary: Listed as an associate sponsor (mécène associé).

record_funding: Its site lists four public partners, the Ministère de la Culture, the Région Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes, the Métropole de Lyon and the Ville de Lyon, then Groupe Partouche, Grand Casino de Lyon Le Pharaon as 'partenaire historique', Esker as 'mécène officiel' and Société Générale and LPA Mobilités as 'mécènes associés'. The pages read did not state amounts.

on_record.summary: Its logo appears among the backers of the extension (2023).

record_funding: A private foundation: for its 4 million euro extension, the Région, the Département and the state gave 500,000 euros each, Groupe Dassault 1 million euros, president Adrien Maeght 500,000 euros, ten individual patrons 500,000 euros together, Triverio Construction 150,000 euros, the Société des Amis 65,000 euros and Saint-Gobain 20,000 euros (The Art Newspaper France, 9 January 2023). The pages read did not state its yearly budget for recent years.

on_record.summary: BRD Groupe Société Générale, its Romanian bank, was a sponsor in October 2023.

record_funding: Romanian Ministry of Culture funds it, with RON 500,000 for 2024 acquisitions. Sponsors include AQUA Carpatica, Greentek Lighting, Crama Oprișor, Molotow, UniCredit Bank and BRD Groupe Société Générale.

on_record.summary: Its corporate foundation is listed as a founding patron.

record_funding: A public establishment paid by the state and the City of Paris. In the 2023 accounts its income was 117,296 thousand euros: 43,208 thousand euros of Ministry of Culture core grant, 16,785 thousand euros of other earmarked public money and 35,463 thousand euros of own income (annual performance report for the Culture budget, 2023). Founder patrons listed are the Fondation d'entreprise Société Générale and the Fondation Bettencourt Schueller.

on_record.summary: One of the corporate supporters named for 2025-26.

record_funding: IWM, the five-site group that includes IWM London, had total income of £79.010m in 2025-26: Grant-in-Aid from the Department for Culture, Media and Sport £35.564m (44%), admissions at its paid sites £18.261m, commercial income £11.681m, fees £6.553m and external grants, donations and sponsorship £4.518m. Corporate supporters named for the year include BAE Systems and Bloomberg Philanthropies.

on_record.summary: Is listed as one of the museum's donors.

record_funding: Federal and private money fund it; private gifts were about 63 percent of USD 126M FY2025 revenue. Jeff Bezos, Boeing, RTX, Lockheed Martin and Northrop Grumman Foundation are donors.
Artist-founded non-profit (Bosco Sodi, 2014); 2026 sponsors: Harp Helú, Home Depot, Teka, Grupo Habita, Tequila 1800, Punta Pájaros, Nirox Foundation.

on_record.summary: A corporate sponsor, shown as an uncaptioned logo on the foundation page.

space_name: Festival International des Arts du Bénin (FInAB)

on_record.summary: Helped fund the 2026 edition. The founder credited MTN’s partnership for its success.

record_funding: Run by Groupe Empire's events arm with Benin government support through its arts fund (FDAC). MTN partnered the 2026 edition, Canal+ Impact 2025. Other partners unnamed; no budget published.

on_record.summary: A gold-level sponsor on the museum's support page.

record_funding: Its support page lists the sponsors Thermos, Contemporary Art Foundation, Sony, Epson and Royal Inn.

on_record.summary: The Schmidt Family Foundation is among its foundation supporters.

record_funding: 2023 revenue US$21.5M (IRS 990), from state and federal agencies, Hawai'i foundations such as Kamehameha Schools, and Hawai'i corporate sponsors.

on_record.summary: Caltex, the fuel retailer now called Ampol, is on the gallery’s Major Gifts roll.

record_funding: City of Ballarat with Creative Victoria. Also named: Ian Potter, Sidney Myer, Buckland, Helen Macpherson Smith, Gandel, McCain, Mars and NAB.

on_record.summary: Is named as a foundation sponsor of the gallery.

record_funding: Christchurch City Council; the Christchurch Art Gallery Foundation raises acquisition funds. Partners are JBWere (foundation partner) and Anthony Harper (major partner), plus hotel, design and drinks suppliers.

on_record.summary: Helps fund the festival, with Air North and Indigenous bodies.

record_funding: Canadian Heritage granted CAD 160,000 for 2025 to 2027; the Town of Inuvik gives the venue and over CAD 30,000 in kind. Indigenous bodies, Air North and Northwestel help; Canada Council refused about CAD 90,000 in 2026.

on_record.summary: Antonio Luis Ferré and Luisa Juliana Rangel are among the museum’s three founding partners, and María Luisa Ferré Rangel is listed as Gran Mecenas.

record_funding: Ferré-Rangel and Fonalledas families, Fundación Ángel Ramos, 700+ individuals. Gala sponsors: Banco Popular, Genera PR (New Fortress Energy, 2023), Puma Energy (2019). 2024-25 Form 990: government grants 58%, earnings <1%.
